ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher within the NS-7 dispute process; no account action against the driver.

rejected_claims.reason: The 4 min 30 s cumulative time inside 200 m runs from the recorded arrival at 13:01:10 [F2], and the 3 min 15 s stationarity began only at 13:02:25 [F3]; NS-1(iii) measures the wait as >3 min from the arrival confirmation/tap until cancellation, and that post-tap interval was 175 s = 2 min 55 s [F6], below the 3:01 threshold [NS-1]. Both figures on which D2 relies therefore do not satisfy the clause.

The 4 min 30 s gap between the recorded arrival and the cancellation [F5][F4] is not the NS-1(iii) measure; the requirement is a >3 min wait at the pickup counted from the arrival flag, and only 2 min 55 s elapsed within 200 m after the 13:02:45 tap before the 13:05:40 cancellation [F6][F4][NS-1]. The driver's own message 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' is a statement that cannot cure the shortfall, since the system timeline controls [F11][F6][NS-1].

The tap at 13:02:45 [F6] does establish NS-1(i), but the claimed 'waiting >3 minutes' element is contradicted by the timeline: only 2 min 55 s of in-radius time remained after the tap until cancellation [F6][F4], so the stay did not meet NS-1(iii) [NS-1].

The contention that condition (i) fails because the tap field is null is not accepted; the timeline records the tap at 13:02:45 while 41 m from the pickup [F6][F1], and this arrival confirmation satisfies NS-1(i) and (ii). The ruling does not rest on the null-field conflict [F7], so this limb of C3 is rejected as immaterial [NS-1].
